editions.text:
The station logged 90 feeder visits and 17 species, marking a quiet day compared to the recent seven-day average of over 200 visits. This low volume aligns with the period following the replacement of the problematic seed feeder on September 13, which had disrupted detection reliability. Despite the reduced physical traffic, the acoustic record remained robust with 300 detections, indicating that regulars such as the Carolina Wren, Northern Cardinal, and Tufted Titmouse continued to frequent the area.

The absence of Mourning Doves, a regular visitor on six of the last seven days, stands out as a notable gap in an otherwise consistent roster. The day’s visual highlights were led by Tufted Titmice and House Finches, whose activity concentrated in specific bursts rather than sustained visits. Eastern Phoebe and White-breasted Nuthatch also appeared, with the latter confirmed in the highlights as visiting the feeders.

The final record of the day was a Carolina Wren arriving one minute after sunset. The day sits below the weekly average in visits but maintains the consistent presence of core species seen throughout the past week.
